results.title: Hyundai Is Spending $26 Billion to Buy Back a Margin It Already Had
results.content: That is the business model observation, and it is not a flattering one for the “growth” framing. The tariff has converted a variable, externally imposed cost into the single largest determinant of Hyundai’s profitability. Management cannot negotiate it, cannot hedge it, and cannot forecast it. What it can do is spend capital to make the cost stop applying. A vehicle assembled in Georgia does not pay the 15 percent. [...] The Metaplant itself is a $7.6 billion assembly campus inside a $12.6 billion Georgia footprint that includes a $4.3 billion battery joint venture with LG Energy Solution. Georgia put up roughly $2.1 billion in incentives, making it the largest public development project in state history. Hyundai counts 8,500 direct jobs on site at the 500,000-unit configuration plus close to 6,900 more at nearby suppliers. The plant currently builds the Ioniq 5, the Ioniq 9 and, since June 2026, the Kia [...] Now the money. Hyundai reported a tariff hit of KRW 860 billion in the first quarter of 2026 and roughly KRW 900 billion in the second, per the company’s own earnings call. That is KRW 1.76 trillion in six months, or a little over $1.1 billion at the quarter’s average rate of 1,502 won to the dollar.

results.content: already operating — Hyundai Motor Manufacturing Alabama (HMMA) in Montgomery, which opened in 2005 and can produce up to 400,000 vehicles per year, and the Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America (HMGMA) near Ellabell, Georgia, which opened in March 2025 with stated capacity of 500,000 EV and hybrid vehicles per year — are central to that strategy. Background on the HMMA and HMGMA plant capacities is available from WardsAuto's coverage of the North America product rollout. [...] Not automatically, but structurally yes over time. A vehicle assembled in Alabama or Georgia does not face the 15% Korean import tariff, which means Hyundai can either price it more competitively than an imported equivalent or capture more margin on the same sticker price. Currently, most Hyundai models sold in the US are manufactured in South Korea, with the Alabama plant producing the Santa Fe, Tucson, Santa Cruz, and Genesis GV70.
